summary: One of many. Unlike a checkbox, it cannot be unticked once ticked.

pairs.dont: Offer a radio group with no default and no way to choose nothing.
pairs.do: Either preselect a sensible default, or add an explicit "None" option.
pairs.why: A radio cannot be unticked by the person who ticked it. Without a default or a None, someone who clicks by accident is stuck with a value they never wanted and no way back.

pairs.dont: Use a radio group for options that are not mutually exclusive.
pairs.why: The control is a promise about the shape of the choice. A radio says picking this un-picks that, and if that is not true the form will fight people.

pairs.dont: Use two radios for on and off.
pairs.do: Use a Switch, or a single Checkbox.
pairs.why: "On / Off" as two radios takes twice the space to say the same thing, and makes the reader compare two labels to find the one difference.

pairs.do: Use Select past about seven options.
pairs.why: Radios are for a set you can take in at a glance and compare. Past that they are a list that happens to be circular, and a Select costs one click to show the same thing.

pairs.dont: Order the options by how they arrived in the API.
pairs.do: Order them by what they mean — severity, frequency, or least to most.
pairs.why: People read a radio group as a scale whether or not you intended one. An arbitrary order invites them to infer a ranking that is not there.

a11y: Radix renders a real radiogroup: arrow keys move between options and wrap, and the group is a single tab stop.
The group needs a name — wrap it in a Field with a FieldLabel, or give the RadioGroup an aria-label.
aria-invalid goes on the item, and colours the border and focus ring together.
